name: Shakti septal ('pleasure center') signal, two coils taking turns every 0.5 s (project layout)
summary: A project layout built on Murphy's Shakti septal signal: one coil over the top of each parietal lobe, taking turns twice a second. The vendor's 8-coil septal file switches between its two stereo channels at that rate, but each channel has coils on both sides of the head, and the vendor says the signal 'has not been tested with human or animal subjects'.
setting: Quiet room, eyes closed, relaxed. Two coils: CP1 over the top of the left parietal lobe and CP2 over the right; the other six stay unused.
schedule: At most weekly; the vendor warns not to over-use it.
notes: The vendor's 8-coil septal file 'alternates between the left and right stereo channels twice each second' (8_coil_septal_consent.htm). Those channels are not head sides: 'Each side of the head gets two pairs' (getting_started_basic.htm). The page asks for a symmetrical 8-coil layout and names the top of the parietal lobes as 'Another place that lends itself to this signal'. This program is this project's own design: two coils, CP1 on the left and CP2 on the right, take turns every 0.5 s for 20 min. Switching between one left and one right coil is not what the vendor's file does. The waveform has no source: the vendor says only that the signal has 'very low frequencies' and 'requires a higher volume than the others' (septum_consent.htm, Important note). The program plays this project's amygdala stand-in slowed down: a rising sweep from 1 to 6 Hz, 230 points of 3 ms (0.69 s), then 4 s of silence. A sweep is longer than a 0.5-s turn, so each one is cut between the two coils. The 20 min are this project's choice. murphy-shakti-septal-horizontal plays both coils together. Field strength: the vendor gives sound-card volume settings only (65% for men and 42% for women on a PCI card, 100% and 85% otherwise). The 1 uT default is this project's. This program's setting is the peak field 20 mm in front of each coil. Two vendor pages say: 'This is a new signal. It has not been tested with human or animal subjects.' (sexual_effects.htm; 8_coil_septal_consent.htm). A third says 'tested with only a few human and no animal subjects' (septum_consent.htm). Independent sham-controlled tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005, double-blind; Gendle & McGrath 2012, where the experimenter knew the condition). The vendor: 'This signal is not a treatment for any medical condition' (pleasure_center.htm). Not for people with epilepsy; stop if it is unpleasant.
source: Murphy, Shakti and the brain's pleasure center – the septum https://www.god-helmet.com/wp/pleasure_center.htm ; Murphy, Shakti demo: Septum signal https://www.god-helmet.com/wp/winshakti/demo/shakti_demo/septum_consent.htm ; Murphy, Shakti demo: Sexual effects https://www.god-helmet.com/wp/winshakti/demo/shakti_demo/sexual_effects.htm ; Murphy, Shakti demo: Understanding the 8 Coil Shakti (fast and slow alternation) https://www.god-helmet.com/wp/winshakti/demo/shakti_demo/rot_principles.htm ; Murphy, Shakti demo: What are 'Rapid' and 'High-Speed' signals? (3-ms points, 4-s latency) https://www.god-helmet.com/wp/winshakti/demo/shakti_demo/rapid_&_high_speed_signals.htm ; Murphy, Shakti demo: Safety – how often https://www.god-helmet.com/wp/winshakti/demo/shakti_demo/how_often_is_safe.htm ; Granqvist et al. 2005, Neurosci Lett 379:1 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15849873/ ; Gendle & McGrath 2012, Percept Mot Skills 114:217 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22582690/
